note: Lab H30 (2026-10-13), round 1 long video: 'C1 Advanced Vocabulary: PERSONALITY', episode 1. Patterned on the small-channel breakout (i-Speak English, 'C1 Advanced Vocabulary PERSONALITY', 50,587 views in 52 days), with our own spin: each part starts from the plain word a learner already says (friendly, shy, rude, lazy, stubborn, honest, proud, kind) and gives five advanced words for it with the difference between them and one example each; two quick tests and a repeat-after-me block per part. No exam coaching. The first advanced word is on screen and spoken in the first 5 seconds; the search phrase 'C1 advanced vocabulary' is said in the first 30 seconds.

beats.speech: Don't just say friendly. Say affable. This is C1 advanced vocabulary for personality: forty advanced words to describe people, each one next to the plain word you already use.

beats.label: friendly
beats.speech: Part one. You say friendly. Here are five advanced words, and the difference between them.

card.headline: Affable
card.meaning: friendly, relaxed and easy to talk to; rather formal
card.example: "The affable host made every guest feel welcome."

beats.speech: Affable. It means friendly, relaxed and easy to talk to. It is rather formal. "The affable host made every guest feel welcome."

card.headline: Amiable
card.meaning: pleasant and friendly in a calm, gentle way
card.example: "He is an amiable man who never argues."

beats.speech: Amiable. It means pleasant and friendly in a calm, gentle way. "He is an amiable man who never argues."

card.headline: Gregarious
card.meaning: very sociable; happiest with other people, especially in groups
card.example: "My gregarious sister talks to everyone at a party."

beats.speech: Gregarious. It means very sociable: happiest with other people, especially in groups. "My gregarious sister talks to everyone at a party."

card.headline: Genial
card.meaning: cheerful, warm and kind to everyone
card.example: "Our genial neighbour always waves and smiles."

beats.speech: Genial. It means cheerful, warm and kind to everyone. "Our genial neighbour always waves and smiles."

card.headline: Approachable
card.meaning: easy to talk to, even when the person is important or busy
card.example: "The professor is approachable, so just ask her."

beats.speech: Approachable. It means easy to talk to, even when the person is important or busy. "The professor is approachable, so just ask her."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: Very sociable; happiest with other people, especially in groups: ___
card.answer: Very sociable; happiest with other people, especially in groups: gregarious

beats.speech: Which word is it? Very sociable; happiest with other people, especially in groups. Gregarious, or amiable? | Gregarious. My gregarious sister talks to everyone at a party.

card.headline: Fill the gap
card.question: Don't be afraid of the director. She is ___.
card.answer: Don't be afraid of the director. She is approachable.

beats.speech: Fill the gap. Don't be afraid of the director. She is blank. Approachable, or gregarious? | Approachable. Don't be afraid of the director. She is approachable. She is important, but easy to talk to.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
The affable host made every guest feel welcome.
He is an amiable man who never argues.
My gregarious sister talks to everyone at a party.
Our genial neighbour always waves and smiles.
The professor is approachable, so just ask her.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | The affable host made every guest feel welcome. | He is an amiable man who never argues. | My gregarious sister talks to everyone at a party. | Our genial neighbour always waves and smiles. | The professor is approachable, so just ask her.

beats.label: shy
beats.speech: Part two. You say shy. Here are five advanced words, and the difference between them.

card.headline: Diffident
card.meaning: shy and not confident about yourself or your abilities
card.example: "He was too diffident to speak up in meetings."

beats.speech: Diffident. It means shy and not confident about yourself or your abilities. "He was too diffident to speak up in meetings."

card.headline: Introverted
card.meaning: quiet, and happier alone or in a small group
card.example: "She is introverted and avoids big parties."

beats.speech: Introverted. It means quiet, and happier alone or in a small group. "She is introverted and avoids big parties."

card.headline: Timid
card.meaning: shy and nervous; easily frightened
card.example: "The timid boy hid behind his mother."

beats.speech: Timid. It means shy and nervous. Easily frightened. "The timid boy hid behind his mother."

card.headline: Reticent
card.meaning: unwilling to talk about something; a formal word
card.example: "He is reticent about his private life."

beats.speech: Reticent. It means unwilling to talk about something. It is a formal word. "He is reticent about his private life."

card.headline: Self-effacing
card.meaning: not wanting attention or praise; modest
card.example: "The self-effacing winner thanked her whole team."

beats.speech: Self-effacing. It means not wanting attention or praise. Modest. "The self-effacing winner thanked her whole team."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: Not wanting attention or praise: ___
card.answer: Not wanting attention or praise: self-effacing

beats.speech: Which word is it? Not wanting attention or praise. Timid, or self-effacing? | Self-effacing. The self-effacing winner thanked her whole team.

card.headline: Fill the gap
card.question: The minister was ___ about his plans.
card.answer: The minister was reticent about his plans.

beats.speech: Fill the gap. The minister was blank about his plans. Reticent, or timid? | Reticent. The minister was reticent about his plans. He was unwilling to talk about them.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
He was too diffident to speak up in meetings.
She is introverted and avoids big parties.
The timid boy hid behind his mother.
He is reticent about his private life.
The self-effacing winner thanked her whole team.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | He was too diffident to speak up in meetings. | She is introverted and avoids big parties. | The timid boy hid behind his mother. | He is reticent about his private life. | The self-effacing winner thanked her whole team.

beats.label: rude
beats.speech: Part three. You say rude. Here are five advanced words, and the difference between them.

card.headline: Abrupt
card.meaning: speaking in a short, quick way that seems unfriendly
card.example: "Sorry if I was abrupt on the phone."

beats.speech: Abrupt. It means speaking in a short, quick way that seems unfriendly. "Sorry if I was abrupt on the phone."

card.headline: Blunt
card.meaning: saying exactly what you think, without trying to be polite
card.example: "To be blunt, your plan will not work."

beats.speech: Blunt. It means saying exactly what you think, without trying to be polite. "To be blunt, your plan will not work."

card.headline: Tactless
card.meaning: saying things that hurt people, without thinking first
card.example: "It was tactless to ask about her age."

beats.speech: Tactless. It means saying things that hurt people, without thinking first. "It was tactless to ask about her age."

card.headline: Condescending
card.meaning: treating people as if they were less intelligent than you
card.example: "Don't use that condescending tone with me."

beats.speech: Condescending. It means treating people as if they were less intelligent than you. "Don't use that condescending tone with me."

card.headline: Obnoxious
card.meaning: extremely unpleasant, often in a loud way
card.example: "An obnoxious passenger shouted at the staff."

beats.speech: Obnoxious. It means extremely unpleasant, often in a loud way. "An obnoxious passenger shouted at the staff."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: Treating people as if they were less intelligent than you: ___
card.answer: Treating people as if they were less intelligent than you: condescending

beats.speech: Which word is it? Treating people as if they were less intelligent than you. Blunt, or condescending? | Condescending. Don't use that condescending tone with me.

card.headline: Fill the gap
card.question: It was ___ to ask how much he earns.
card.answer: It was tactless to ask how much he earns.

beats.speech: Fill the gap. It was blank to ask how much he earns. Tactless, or abrupt? | Tactless. It was tactless to ask how much he earns. A question like that can hurt, and the speaker did not think first.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Sorry if I was abrupt on the phone.
To be blunt, your plan will not work.
It was tactless to ask about her age.
Don't use that condescending tone with me.
An obnoxious passenger shouted at the staff.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Sorry if I was abrupt on the phone. | To be blunt, your plan will not work. | It was tactless to ask about her age. | Don't use that condescending tone with me. | An obnoxious passenger shouted at the staff.

beats.label: lazy
beats.speech: Part four. You say lazy. Here are five advanced words, and the difference between them.

card.headline: Idle
card.meaning: not working, and not wanting to work
card.example: "He is an idle student who never does his homework."

beats.speech: Idle. It means not working, and not wanting to work. "He is an idle student who never does his homework."

card.headline: Indolent
card.meaning: lazy by nature, avoiding all effort; a formal word
card.example: "An indolent worker waits to be told what to do."

beats.speech: Indolent. It means lazy by nature, avoiding all effort. It is a formal word. "An indolent worker waits to be told what to do."

card.headline: Lethargic
card.meaning: having no energy and slow to do anything; how you feel, not who you are
card.example: "The heat made everyone lethargic."

beats.speech: Lethargic. It means having no energy and being slow to do anything. It is how you feel, not who you are. "The heat made everyone lethargic."

card.headline: Complacent
card.meaning: so pleased with yourself that you stop trying; lazy because of success
card.example: "After three wins, the team became complacent."

beats.speech: Complacent. It means so pleased with yourself that you stop trying: lazy because of success. "After three wins, the team became complacent."

card.headline: Apathetic
card.meaning: not interested, and not caring enough to act; lazy because you do not care
card.example: "He is apathetic about his studies."

beats.speech: Apathetic. It means not interested, and not caring enough to act: lazy because you do not care. "He is apathetic about his studies."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: So pleased with yourself that you stop trying: ___
card.answer: So pleased with yourself that you stop trying: complacent

beats.speech: Which word is it? So pleased with yourself that you stop trying. Complacent, or lethargic? | Complacent. After three wins, the team became complacent.

card.headline: Fill the gap
card.question: I have a cold and I feel so ___ today.
card.answer: I have a cold and I feel so lethargic today.

beats.speech: Fill the gap. I have a cold and I feel so blank today. Idle, or lethargic? | Lethargic. I have a cold and I feel so lethargic today. You have no energy today, but that is not who you are.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
He is an idle student who never does his homework.
An indolent worker waits to be told what to do.
The heat made everyone lethargic.
After three wins, the team became complacent.
He is apathetic about his studies.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | He is an idle student who never does his homework. | An indolent worker waits to be told what to do. | The heat made everyone lethargic. | After three wins, the team became complacent. | He is apathetic about his studies.

beats.label: stubborn
beats.speech: Part five. You say stubborn. Here are five advanced words, and the difference between them.

card.headline: Strong-willed
card.meaning: determined to do what you want; often said with respect
card.example: "Our strong-willed daughter never gives up."

beats.speech: Strong-willed. It means determined to do what you want. Often said with respect. "Our strong-willed daughter never gives up."

card.headline: Headstrong
card.meaning: determined to do things your own way, ignoring advice
card.example: "He was too headstrong to listen to his doctor."

beats.speech: Headstrong. It means determined to do things your own way, ignoring advice. "He was too headstrong to listen to his doctor."

card.headline: Obstinate
card.meaning: refusing to change your mind, even when you are wrong
card.example: "She remained obstinate, despite all the evidence."

beats.speech: Obstinate. It means refusing to change your mind, even when you are wrong. "She remained obstinate, despite all the evidence."

card.headline: Inflexible
card.meaning: unwilling to change plans, rules or opinions
card.example: "My boss is inflexible about working hours."

beats.speech: Inflexible. It means unwilling to change plans, rules or opinions. "My boss is inflexible about working hours."

card.headline: Tenacious
card.meaning: never giving up; the positive side of stubborn
card.example: "A tenacious lawyer fought the case for years."

beats.speech: Tenacious. It means never giving up. The positive side of stubborn. "A tenacious lawyer fought the case for years."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: Never giving up; the positive side of stubborn: ___
card.answer: Never giving up; the positive side of stubborn: tenacious

beats.speech: Which word is it? Never giving up; the positive side of stubborn. Obstinate, or tenacious? | Tenacious. A tenacious lawyer fought the case for years.

card.headline: Fill the gap
card.question: He ignored every warning and did it his own way. He is so ___.
card.answer: He ignored every warning and did it his own way. He is so headstrong.

beats.speech: Fill the gap. He ignored every warning and did it his own way. He is so blank. Headstrong, or inflexible? | Headstrong. He ignored every warning and did it his own way. He is so headstrong. He would not listen to anyone.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Our strong-willed daughter never gives up.
He was too headstrong to listen to his doctor.
She remained obstinate, despite all the evidence.
My boss is inflexible about working hours.
A tenacious lawyer fought the case for years.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Our strong-willed daughter never gives up. | He was too headstrong to listen to his doctor. | She remained obstinate, despite all the evidence. | My boss is inflexible about working hours. | A tenacious lawyer fought the case for years.

beats.label: honest
beats.speech: Part six. You say honest. Here are five advanced words, and the difference between them.

card.headline: Frank
card.meaning: honest and direct, even when it is uncomfortable
card.example: "Can I be frank with you about your work?"

beats.speech: Frank. It means honest and direct, even when it is uncomfortable. "Can I be frank with you about your work?"

card.headline: Candid
card.meaning: open and honest about difficult or private things
card.example: "She was candid about her past mistakes."

beats.speech: Candid. It means open and honest about difficult or private things. "She was candid about her past mistakes."

card.headline: Forthright
card.meaning: saying what you think clearly and with confidence
card.example: "He gave a forthright answer to every question."

beats.speech: Forthright. It means saying what you think clearly and with confidence. "He gave a forthright answer to every question."

card.headline: Upfront
card.meaning: honest from the start, hiding nothing; informal
card.example: "Please be upfront about the total cost."

beats.speech: Upfront. It means honest from the start, hiding nothing. It is informal. "Please be upfront about the total cost."

card.headline: Principled
card.meaning: always doing what you believe is right; honest in actions, not only in words
card.example: "A principled judge cannot be bought."

beats.speech: Principled. It means always doing what you believe is right: honest in actions, not only in words. "A principled judge cannot be bought."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: Always doing what you believe is right: ___
card.answer: Always doing what you believe is right: principled

beats.speech: Which word is it? Always doing what you believe is right. Forthright, or principled? | Principled. A principled judge cannot be bought.

card.headline: Fill the gap
card.question: In the interview she was ___ about her illness.
card.answer: In the interview she was candid about her illness.

beats.speech: Fill the gap. In the interview she was blank about her illness. Candid, or principled? | Candid. In the interview she was candid about her illness. She spoke openly about something private.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
Can I be frank with you about your work?
She was candid about her past mistakes.
He gave a forthright answer to every question.
Please be upfront about the total cost.
A principled judge cannot be bought.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | Can I be frank with you about your work? | She was candid about her past mistakes. | He gave a forthright answer to every question. | Please be upfront about the total cost. | A principled judge cannot be bought.

beats.label: too proud
beats.speech: Part seven. You say too proud. Here are five advanced words, and the difference between them.

card.headline: Conceited
card.meaning: too proud of yourself and of what you can do
card.example: "She is talented, but not at all conceited."

beats.speech: Conceited. It means too proud of yourself and of what you can do. "She is talented, but not at all conceited."

card.headline: Vain
card.meaning: too proud of how you look
card.example: "He is so vain that he looks in every mirror."

beats.speech: Vain. It means too proud of how you look. "He is so vain that he looks in every mirror."

card.headline: Smug
card.meaning: too pleased with yourself, and showing it
card.example: "Wipe that smug smile off your face."

beats.speech: Smug. It means too pleased with yourself, and showing it. "Wipe that smug smile off your face."

card.headline: Pompous
card.meaning: too serious and full of your own importance
card.example: "The pompous official made everyone wait."

beats.speech: Pompous. It means too serious and full of your own importance. "The pompous official made everyone wait."

card.headline: Haughty
card.meaning: proud and unfriendly, looking down on other people
card.example: "She gave the waiter a haughty look."

beats.speech: Haughty. It means proud and unfriendly, looking down on other people. "She gave the waiter a haughty look."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: Too proud of how you look: ___
card.answer: Too proud of how you look: vain

beats.speech: Which word is it? Too proud of how you look. Smug, or vain? | Vain. He is so vain that he looks in every mirror.

card.headline: Fill the gap
card.question: He won, and now he is so ___ about it.
card.answer: He won, and now he is so smug about it.

beats.speech: Fill the gap. He won, and now he is so blank about it. Smug, or haughty? | Smug. He won, and now he is so smug about it. He is pleased with himself, and it shows.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
She is talented, but not at all conceited.
He is so vain that he looks in every mirror.
Wipe that smug smile off your face.
The pompous official made everyone wait.
She gave the waiter a haughty look.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | She is talented, but not at all conceited. | He is so vain that he looks in every mirror. | Wipe that smug smile off your face. | The pompous official made everyone wait. | She gave the waiter a haughty look.

beats.label: kind
beats.speech: Part eight. You say kind. Here are five advanced words, and the difference between them.

card.headline: Considerate
card.meaning: thinking about what other people need or feel
card.example: "It was considerate of you to call first."

beats.speech: Considerate. It means thinking about what other people need or feel. "It was considerate of you to call first."

card.headline: Compassionate
card.meaning: feeling for people who suffer, and wanting to help
card.example: "A compassionate nurse sat with him all night."

beats.speech: Compassionate. It means feeling for people who suffer, and wanting to help. "A compassionate nurse sat with him all night."

card.headline: Empathetic
card.meaning: able to understand how another person feels
card.example: "A good teacher is empathetic and patient."

beats.speech: Empathetic. It means able to understand how another person feels. "A good teacher is empathetic and patient."

card.headline: Selfless
card.meaning: caring more about other people than about yourself
card.example: "Her selfless act saved two lives."

beats.speech: Selfless. It means caring more about other people than about yourself. "Her selfless act saved two lives."

card.headline: Altruistic
card.meaning: helping others without wanting anything back; a formal word
card.example: "His motives were not purely altruistic."

beats.speech: Altruistic. It means helping others without wanting anything back. It is a formal word. "His motives were not purely altruistic."

card.headline: Which word is it?
card.question: Able to understand how another person feels: ___
card.answer: Able to understand how another person feels: empathetic

beats.speech: Which word is it? Able to understand how another person feels. Empathetic, or selfless? | Empathetic. A good teacher is empathetic and patient.

card.headline: Fill the gap
card.question: How ___ of you to save me a seat!
card.answer: How considerate of you to save me a seat!

beats.speech: Fill the gap. How blank of you to save me a seat! Considerate, or altruistic? | Considerate. How considerate of you to save me a seat! You thought about what I needed.

card.headline: Repeat after me
card.sentences:
It was considerate of you to call first.
A compassionate nurse sat with him all night.
A good teacher is empathetic and patient.
Her selfless act saved two lives.
His motives were not purely altruistic.

beats.speech: Now say them out loud with me. | It was considerate of you to call first. | A compassionate nurse sat with him all night. | A good teacher is empathetic and patient. | Her selfless act saved two lives. | His motives were not purely altruistic.
Final test. Eight questions, one for each part. Say your answer before the countdown ends.

card.headline: Final test: 1 of 8
card.question: Everyone likes our old doctor; he is always cheerful and ___.
card.answer: Everyone likes our old doctor; he is always cheerful and genial.

beats.speech: Number one. Everyone likes our old doctor; he is always cheerful and blank. Genial, or haughty? | Genial. Everyone likes our old doctor; he is always cheerful and genial.

card.headline: Final test: 2 of 8
card.question: The child was too ___ to say hello.
card.answer: The child was too timid to say hello.

beats.speech: Number two. The child was too blank to say hello. Timid, or blunt? | Timid. The child was too timid to say hello.

card.headline: Final test: 3 of 8
card.question: "That is wrong," she said, and hung up. She was cold and ___.
card.answer: "That is wrong," she said, and hung up. She was cold and abrupt.

beats.speech: Number three. "That is wrong," she said, and hung up. She was cold and blank. Abrupt, or amiable? | Abrupt. "That is wrong," she said, and hung up. She was cold and abrupt.

card.headline: Final test: 4 of 8
card.question: The voters were ___: they did not care who won.
card.answer: The voters were apathetic: they did not care who won.

beats.speech: Number four. The voters were blank: they did not care who won. Apathetic, or tenacious? | Apathetic. The voters were apathetic: they did not care who won.

card.headline: Final test: 5 of 8
card.question: The rules never change. The school is ___.
card.answer: The rules never change. The school is inflexible.

beats.speech: Number five. The rules never change. The school is blank. Inflexible, or candid? | Inflexible. The rules never change. The school is inflexible.

card.headline: Final test: 6 of 8
card.question: Be ___ about the price before we sign.
card.answer: Be upfront about the price before we sign.

beats.speech: Number six. Be blank about the price before we sign. Upfront, or vain? | Upfront. Be upfront about the price before we sign.

card.headline: Final test: 7 of 8
card.question: The professor was ___: he loved the sound of his own voice.
card.answer: The professor was pompous: he loved the sound of his own voice.

beats.speech: Number seven. The professor was blank: he loved the sound of his own voice. Pompous, or selfless? | Pompous. The professor was pompous: he loved the sound of his own voice.

card.headline: Final test: 8 of 8
card.question: The firefighter was ___: she risked her life for a stranger.
card.answer: The firefighter was selfless: she risked her life for a stranger.

beats.speech: Number eight. The firefighter was blank: she risked her life for a stranger. Selfless, or smug? | Selfless. The firefighter was selfless: she risked her life for a stranger.
